cells.tense: You are holding a possibility open without having to make it mean anything yet.
cells.act: let yourself want it, plainly, to yourself
cells.ask: When something pulls at you, admit the pull to yourself in plain words — no plan, no explaining it to anyone, no deciding whether it's allowed. Just the want, said once, privately, whenever it comes.
cells.core:
Within the customs and stories that get handed between people, you can stand in something before it has a name. That is the working state — open, available, each moment a little fresh — and it is not indecision. A person picking up a family recipe, or a song, or a habit of speech, and trying it on before they keep it: that is the shape of it, and the trying is the point.

You can carry something forward without flattening it into a shape it hasn't chosen. The pull to feed next is real, and it is yours to choose. Here is a small way in. When something pulls at you, admit the pull to yourself in plain words — no plan, no explaining, no deciding whether it's allowed. Just the want, said once, privately. That is the beginning of knowing which light you are steering by.

cells.tense: You will keep circling every option, and the future will still refuse to be written on.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Pick a custom or story you keep leaving open. Do it once, this week, in your own way — a word changed, a step dropped, a timing moved — and don't explain the change to anyone.
cells.core:
Inside the customs and stories that get handed along, you stand before every possibility and enter none. Each one is still being weighed, and those hours add up. Round after round, the question is kept open, and the very range you meant to protect starts to feel like no ground under you. The list of options is not the life.

You do not need to settle the whole shape at once. Pick a custom or story you keep leaving open, and do it once, this week, the way only you would — a word changed, a step dropped, a timing moved. Don't announce it. What you actually are will show itself in the act, and one week of it will tell you more than another year of deciding.

cells.tense: You stood at a door once, and it is still behind you, holding you where you are.
cells.act: draw the whole arrangement you are inside, with yourself marked on it
cells.ask: Take one sheet of paper and draw the customs and stories around you — the tables, the sayings, the yearly things — as a simple arrangement, then put a dot where you stand in it. Afterwards, nothing needs deciding.
cells.core:
Within the customs and stories that get passed down, starting fresh is not available right now. You are still present, still showing up, but the part of you that could begin from nothing has gone quiet, and you build from what is left. The work still gets done. It is narrower, and the wider thing you used to reach for from this same spot is not landing.

That narrowness is not the whole picture. Take one sheet and draw the customs and stories around you — tables, sayings, yearly things — as a simple arrangement, then put a dot where you stand in it. Nothing gets decided after. You are seeing where you are in the whole, and a thing seen tends to show a little more of itself.

cells.tense: Doors are opening and closing right now, and you walk through them without seeing you chose.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: The next time a choice comes up — what to join, what to skip, what to continue — stay in it for a breath, then take one small step on purpose rather than by reflex. Only that.
cells.core:
In the space where meaning gets handed between people, options are taken without being seen. You move through customs and stories the way you have before, and the moving looks natural, and no one can tell — most weeks, including you — that anything was being selected at all. The doors are not hidden. They are simply not being looked at.

Enough light for one step is enough for this. The next time a choice comes up — whether to join, skip, or continue — stay in it for one breath, then make that single step on purpose instead of out of reflex. Nothing grand, nothing announced. One step taken with your hand on it is how your say comes back.
